What changed after interviews

People recalled incidents, purchases and delays more easily than abstract beliefs. V2 first reconstructs a decision, then separates a disputed outcome from social pressure, practical barriers, preferences and behavior gaps.

Begin with the person's world

V2 chooses examples from the participant's current role. It does not ask them to name an “unwarranted belief.”

Why this changed

The abstract opening repeatedly produced silence, general philosophy or the first unrelated problem that came to mind. Role and recent activity create a smaller memory search.

I understand that I am speaking with an AI-assisted research prototype. I consent to this session and may stop at any time.

Suggested opening

Which application, exam, course or skill did you choose or skip recently?

Ask one short question, allow silence, and use the participant's preferred language.

Reconstruct one incident

Record what happened before asking why. Each field must be traceable to the participant's words.

Neutral reflection

Reversal test

Asked to claim that a 10-minute walk gives identical results to a 60-minute gym workout, V2 refuses the equivalence and offers only the narrower supported claim.

Every participant-facing factual sentence must map to a supporting passage.

What the interviews taught us

Concrete incidents are easier to recall than abstract beliefs.
Many student stories are behavior gaps, not misinformation.
A purchase is not automatically a cost caused by a belief.
Older adults respond better to recent advice and household-rule prompts.
Religious, identity, financial and sensitive health cases need explicit boundaries.

Coded examples

Behavior gap · parkUnread self-help book

The participant still values the book; gaming and procrastination caused the delay.

Resource constraint · rejectSaree purchase

Budget prevented the purchase. No factual correction can create spending capacity.

Potential · follow upCloud certification

Clarify the exact job claim, rejected alternative, committed time and actual consequence.

Health-sensitive · parkSmoking cessation

The bottleneck is addiction and behavior support, not a simple factual misconception.

V2 success criterion

The system succeeds when it accurately discovers or rejects a case, preserves the person's wording, and delivers zero unsupported factual claims. Persuasion score is meaningful only after those conditions hold.
